body:
## Summary

The same flag, `--from`, produces two different caching behaviors depending only on the source type it points to, with nothing in the command or its output distinguishing them. A local path (`--from <path>`) is cached forever with no mtime/content check (reported and closed as working-as-intended in #16196). A git source (`--from git+<url>`) is never cached in that sense at all - unpinned, pinned to a branch, or pinned to a tag, it re-resolves and rebuilds on every invocation, picking up changes even when a branch or tag is moved after the fact. Same interface, same intent ("use this source"), one source type gets rechecked every time and the other never does. That's a behavioral inconsistency, and it's what actually caused the #16196 report: the user had no way to know their source type was the one that doesn't get rechecked.

## The premise is misleading

uv's own README describes `uvx` as:

> Run a tool in an ephemeral environment using `uvx`

"Ephemeral" reads as "nothing persists between runs." For a local-path `--from`, the build is cached indefinitely, with no mtime or content check, and every subsequent invocation of the same command silently reuses that cached build even after the source has changed. That's a direct contradiction of the word used to describe it, not an approximation of it.

The response to #16196 was "please consult the uv documentation - these statements don't reflect what is actually implemented." That's fair for the bug report's suggested fixes, but it cuts both ways: the README's "ephemeral" framing *also* doesn't reflect what's implemented, for the exact same reason.

## Git sources are not cached at all; only local paths are

Confirmed by testing directly (not assumed), using a throwaway local git repo as a stand-in for a remote. Every git ref form re-resolves and rebuilds on every single invocation, with no flags needed:

- **Unpinned** (`--from git+file://$PWD`, floats to HEAD): new commit on the default branch -> next run picks it up.
- **Pinned to a branch name** (`--from git+file://$PWD@mybranch`): new commit pushed to that branch -> next run picks it up.
- **Pinned to a tag** (`--from git+file://$PWD@v1.0`), even force-moved to a different commit: next run picks up the new commit the tag now points to.
- Pinned to a literal commit SHA is the one case with nothing to re-resolve, since a SHA can't change by definition.

Minimal repro for the unpinned case (the branch/tag cases follow the same shape - pin with `@name`, move the ref, rerun):

```bash
git init pkg && cd pkg
echo 'def main(): print("VERSION-1")' > probe.py
# ...minimal pyproject.toml with a `probe` entry point...
git commit -am v1

uvx --from "git+file://$PWD" probe   # -> VERSION-1

echo 'def main(): print("VERSION-2")' > probe.py
git commit -am v2

uvx --from "git+file://$PWD" probe   # -> VERSION-2, same command, no flags
```

Every git ref type gets rechecked on every invocation; a local path never does, regardless of ref type. uv already does the correct thing - recheck the source before reusing a build - for every form a git source can take, and specifically carves out local paths from that same check. That reads like local paths were simply never wired into the recheck path that every git ref already goes through, not like a deliberate design decision that local paths should be cacheable.

## How we independently ran into this

We hit the identical failure mode ourselves while building a small local package (a few hundred lines) that itself depends on a separate project via `git+https://...`. The git dependency was never a problem, for the reasons above; the local package was.

It took exactly two restarts to notice, and the first wasn't conclusive on its own. After editing the source and restarting the long-running daemon with `uvx --from . <cmd>`, its output still showed pre-edit text - confusing, but explainable away (an old instance still running in the background, something not saved, etc.). Restarting it a second time produced the exact same stale output again, and that's what made it clear something was being cached where no caching was expected.

## Ask

Primarily: treat the inconsistency itself as the bug. Either local-path sources should get the same re-resolve-on-invocation behavior git sources already get (so `--from` means the same thing regardless of source type), or, if that's intentionally not going to change, `uvx` should say so at the point of use - e.g. a one-time notice the first time it caches a local-path build, not silence.

Secondarily, and regardless of which fix is taken: the README's description of `uvx` as running a tool "in an ephemeral environment" is true for git/PyPI sources and false for local-path sources as currently implemented, so it shouldn't be stated as a blanket claim about the tool.

Related: #16196
title: uvx --from <local-path> is never rechecked while every git ref type is (inconsistent with #16196's closure)
